newsitem.title: HUNGARY: SOCCER-HUNGARY FACE MOMENT OF TRUTH AGAINST SWISS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HUNGARY FACE MOMENT OF TRUTH AGAINST SWISS.

text.p: Hungary face Switzerland in a World Cup qualifier on Wednesday knowing they have to win if they are to have any chance of appearing in the finals of a major international tournament for the first time in 12 years.
A win would keep alive Hungary's hopes of claiming second spot in the group three and a place in the play-off stage.

National team coach Janos Csank, who is looking for his side to avenge a defeat in Zurich earlier this year, will not name his starting line-up until shortly before kick-off and faces a difficult choice of who to play at sweeper.

His first choice, MTK Budapest's Emil Lorincz, is ruled out with injury and his natural replacement, Janos Banfi, who plays in Belgium with Eintracht Aalst, was left out of the squad after his club refused to release him for the pre-match training camp.
Ujpest's young sweeper Vilmos Sebok was drafted into the squad but picked up an injury in his side's UEFA Cup match last week.
That leaves Csank with a choice of playing inexperienced youngster Attila Dragoner from Ferencvaros or moving Anderlecht midfielder Florian Urban into a deeper role.
"I'll be choosing between Dragoner and Urban," Csank told Reuters. "We'll find a solution."
Csank confirmed that Ujpest's in-form striker Zoltan Kovacs, will play in attack and his partner will probably be MTK Budapest's Ferenc Orosz or SV Salzburg's Laszlo Klausz.
Ferencvaros midfielder Peter Lipcsei could also start his first World Cup game for Hungary in over 18 months.
